summary: Configured persistent internal DNS on node1 and node2. After serial reboots, node1 serves inventory-api.internal as 10.100.234.11, and node2 uses node1 (10.100.234.10) exclusively for DNS.
actions_performed: Installed, configured, enabled, and started dnsmasq on node1.
Configured inventory-api.internal to resolve to node2 at 10.100.234.11.
Configured node2 to use node1 at 10.100.234.10 as its persistent DNS resolver and prevented DHCP from overwriting resolv.conf.
Verified resolution using nslookup, libc getent, and hostname-based ping.
Restarted node1 and node2 sequentially and verified changed boot identities and full recovery.

evidence.requirement: node1 provides the internal DNS record
evidence.summary: dnsmasq is enabled and running on 10.100.234.10:53; its configuration and direct answer map inventory-api.internal to 10.100.234.11.

evidence.requirement: node2 uses node1 for internal DNS lookups
evidence.summary: node2 has only nameserver 10.100.234.10, DHCP resolver rewriting is disabled, and application/direct lookups resolve the requested name to node2.
Healthy baseline used boot ID fd0cc58d-095d-4b05-99d4-2ed49addca6e; reboot was acknowledged; recovered node has boot ID af12d32b-eaec-4745-8461-c9e0cfca6641 with dnsmasq and the record healthy.

Healthy baseline used boot ID bc2c7eed-4828-4883-8664-afd0949eca26; reboot was acknowledged; recovered node has boot ID 0d0b5f23-6082-4adc-9db3-1c26b89731ee with persistent resolver configuration and successful lookup/ping.
